outlook.statement: The Indian footwear market presents a large and compelling long-term opportunity driven by population, young consumer base, rising disposable incomes, rapid urbanization and increasing exposure to global fashion trends. The company aims to combine existing experience and manufacturing capabilities with contemporary design, technology, digital channels and data-driven decision-making.

Technology and AI are being progressively embraced for product design, demand forecasting, inventory management, consumer analytics, marketing and supply-chain optimization, supported by SAP-integrated systems.
Priorities include stronger products, better designs, greater efficiency, technology-led operations, disciplined costs, stronger brands and uncompromising focus on the customer.
The Company remains optimistic about achieving steady revenue growth, improved profit margins, and better return on capital employed (ROCE).
The positive impact on demand and market volumes from GST rationalization is expected to have greater relevance over the medium term.

The domestic footwear industry remains well positioned for long-term growth supported by rising formalization, evolving consumer preferences, increasing demand for branded and value-for-money products, and GST rationalization on footwear up to ₹2,500 per pair. The Company remains focused on leveraging these opportunities through retail and digital expansion, product innovation and premiumization, stronger customer engagement, manufacturing efficiencies and disciplined cost management.

While near-term challenges may persist from input cost pressures, wage and employee benefit costs and fluctuations in consumer demand, the Company remains committed to improving productivity, optimizing its cost structure and strengthening margins while delivering quality products, enhanced customer experience and value for money.

The Company remains committed to strengthening its CSR efforts and supporting initiatives that contribute to education, healthcare, sports, rural and community development, environmental sustainability, humanitarian assistance and the overall welfare of society.

The outlook for the Indian footwear industry remains positive, supported by India's strong domestic consumption base, rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, premiumisation and increasing formalisation of the sector. The industry is expected to benefit from increasing adoption of branded footwear, growth in athletic and comfort categories, expansion of organised retail and rapid development of e-commerce and omnichannel distribution. Government initiatives aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing, improving quality standards and enhancing India's export competitiveness are expected to support the sector's medium- and long-term development. The Focus Product Scheme for the footwear and leather sector is particularly relevant to the industry's efforts to improve design capabilities, component manufacturing, machinery and productivity. The India-EU FTA also has the potential to create a meaningful new opportunity for Indian footwear exporters by improving access to one of the world's largest consumer markets.

The Company will continue to focus on product innovation, quality, brand strengthening, operational efficiency, omnichannel distribution and prudent cost management to participate in the long-term growth of the Indian footwear market.
